function: Exclude (above_phy): the multi-agent DRL learns only UAV trajectories and the charging-time split (p. 5, p. 6); IRS phases and UAV association are non-learned (p. 8, Theorem 1).
notes: above_phy. p. 5: "we first design a multi-agent DRL-based algorithm to learn UAV trajectories and charging time allocation policies. Then, we propose a low-complexity strategy to obtain IRS phase shift matrices and UAV association factor." p. 6: "The action space consists of two subsets of UAV coordinates and WPT time allocation strategies." p. 8: Algorithm 1 line 7 and Theorem 1 obtain the IRS phases by closed-form phase alignment, so the RIS is not learned. The abstract wording "jointly optimize ... phase shift matrices of IRSs" overstates what the DRL learns. UAV trajectory and time-slot scheduling are above the physical layer; no learned control of transmit power, beams or RIS. Borderline for the reviewer: if the charging-time split counts as resource allocation of an aerial link (exception of above_phy), the work would be area 6 with RIS present, custom Rician/LoS channel (p. 4), TE/RA and SCR/MADRL-PPO baselines (p. 10), complexity in Theorem 2 (p. 8), no code link.
